title: Smoothed throughput contracts and reservation fallback adapter
author: Priya Sethi
release_notes: Introduce smoothed throughput contract semantics and a reservation fallback adapter to reduce oscillation in dedicated fleet reservations. Adds new telemetry and a safe rollout plan; no user-facing API changes aside from an opt-in config flag.
description:
Motivation: Fleet reservations can oscillate under bursty tenant workloads and discrete reservation semantics. This creates transient SLA miss windows despite ample capacity. The goal of this PR is to introduce a smoothing layer for throughput contracts and a fallback adapter for reservations so that canaries and rollouts experience minimal churn while preserving throughput guarantees.

Summary of changes:
1) Add a reservoir-weighted smoothing algorithm for per-tenant throughput contracts (pkg/dedicated/contract/smoother.go). The smoother computes an exponential moving reservation target using request-rate and slot-utilization signals with separate short/long windows to capture bursts without overreacting to transient spikes.
2) Introduce reservation_fallback_adapter (pkg/dedicated/reservation/fallback_adapter.go) which mediates between desired reservation and actual slot allocation. When the adapter detects allocation lag or shortfall it applies a graceful fallback policy rather than immediately revoking or force-expanding reservations.
3) Autoscaler integration: new smoothing_policy implementation in the autoscaler decider replaces abrupt commit changes with delta-limited adjustments.
4) Telemetry: new metrics emitted (redwood.dedicated.contract.smoothed_target, redwood.dedicated.contract.raw_signal, redwood.dedicated.reservation.fallback_events) and per-tenant percentiles for smoothed utilization.
5) Operator tooling: ctl migrate_reservations can backfill smoothing state from recent utilization history; a safe, idempotent migration is provided.
6) Tests and perf: added unit tests and a dedicated e2e prow job that runs a 10-minute bursty workload to validate stability and headroom preservation.

Design notes and rationale:
- Smoothing uses dual-window aggregation (short=18s, long=180s by default) and a reservoir weight to bias towards long-term commitments when available. The dual-window avoids chasing short transients but still responds within bounded latency for sustained changes.
- The fallback adapter exposes three modes: NO_FALLBACK (legacy), SOFT_FALLBACK (preferred default), and AGGRESSIVE (for constrained clusters). SOFT_FALLBACK will throttle new allocations by a small margin, shift queued requests into warm-pool, and increment a fallback counter to show up in dashboards.
- This approach separates the responsibility of contract computation from allocator enforcement so downstream allocators can implement conservative allocation strategies without changing contract semantics.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind config flag dedicated.contracts.smoothing.enabled=false by default.
- Nightly canary on a single dedicated pool for 48h with telemetry baseline comparison.
- If telemetry shows below-1% increase in 99th percentile latency and no >5% delta in throughput for the canary tenants, progressively enable for 30% of dedicated pools, then 100% in 24h.

Migration:
- ctl migrate_reservations --smoothing-backfill reads 12h of utilization and seeds smoother reservoir; safe to run concurrently.

Metrics and observability:
- Added Grafana dashboard snapshot at observability/dashboards/dedicated_utilization.json.
- Emit structured fallback events to tracing to correlate with tenant latency regressions.

Testing and CI:
- Added unit tests covering corner cases for very sparse tenants and high-churn tenants.
- Added a perf script scripts/perf/bench_throughput_smoother.sh that reproduces an oscillating reservation pattern; results show 18-34% reduction in reservation churn under synthetic workloads.
- CI: new prow job deploy/prow/jobs/dedicated-e2e.yaml that runs the e2e smoke + perf harness; first run had a flaky assertion and was fixed by increasing test harness warmup.

Review conversation summary: "Anil Kapoor: Please clarify how the fallback adapter interacts with the warm-pool. Response: The adapter attempts to shift soft-fallback demand into the warm-pool by signaling warm-pool pre-warm hooks; if warm-pool capacity insufficient we emit a fallback_event and apply request-level throttling. Anil: Add a telemetry gauge for fallback_event.rate. Addressed in commit 4. Sofia Martinez: Add integration test that simulates allocation lag and verify no double-counting of reservation. Response: Added dedicated e2e job and a unit test simulating allocator latency in smoothing_policy_test.go. Sofia: Concerned about operator migration safety. Response: ctl migrate_reservations is idempotent and has dry-run flag; included docs/runbooks/reservation-fallback.md with instructions. Eliot Zhang: Tests look good; can we add a short note on how this impacts percent-of-capacity billing? Response: This PR does not change billing semantics; smoothing only influences allocation timing. Eliot approved and requested a perf run; perf showed expected improvement." 

Approvals and outcome:
- After two rounds of review and a successful e2e run the PR was squash-merged into main on 2026-01-21.

Impact and follow-ups:
- Ops: Recommend enabling smoothing in a limited set of nondestructive pools and monitor redwood.dedicated.reservation.fallback_events and 99th percentile latency.
- Follow-up work: add a cluster-level adaptive reservoir tuner (ENG-2101) and a Prometheus alert for sustained fallback_event rate.

Related work: ENG-1973 implemented a KV-cache aware occupancy sampler that provided the initial utilization signal used by the smoother.

Links: runbook: docs/runbooks/reservation-fallback.md, migration CLI: cmd/ctl/migrate_reservations, perf script: scripts/perf/bench_throughput_smoother.sh.

notes: This PR intentionally keeps the smoothing policy opt-in to limit blast radius. Config defaults are conservative; operators should follow the rollout plan in the runbook.
